newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-BOON DISAPPOINTED AS SHIELD MATCH DRAWN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BOON DISAPPOINTED AS SHIELD MATCH DRAWN.

text.p: Tasmania captain David Boon said on Monday said he was disappointed Victoria had not tried to force a result on the fourth and final day of their Sheffield match at Bellerive Oval.
Boon set Victoria a winning target of 362 in a minimum of 70 overs after declaring his side's second innings on 311 for two late in Monday's first session.

The match ended 30 minutes ahead of the scheduled close with Victoria on 204 for three. Boon told reporters he felt Victoria, captained by his former Australia team mate Dean Jones, had not chased the target hard enough.
"I was extremely disappointed that there was no effort at all to try and make a game of that," Boon said.
Jones, leading Victoria in the absence of Australia leg-spinner Shane Warne, said his side had given up the chase but argued it had been too big to reach in the time available.
"I just thought it was an unrealistic chance," Jones told reporters. "In my career I've never seen anyone get 360 in that many overs."
Victorian opening batsmen Warren Ayres and Brad Hodge began aggresively by taking 13 off the first over before Hodge fell for Victoria to be 20 for one at lunch.
The flow of runs dried up in the second session after Jones was dismissed for 36.
Tasmania resumed at 161 without loss before opener Jamie Cox was dismissed for 132. Fellow opener Dene Hills became the sixth century-maker in the match and was on 124 when Boon declared.
Ayres went on to score 56 while Ian Harvey was 62 not out at the close.
